text:
John Carlson is having the kind of November that makes a 36-year-old look like he found something. He reached 800 career points with a career-best five-point night in Buffalo, then had three assists against Washington, the team he played 1,143 games for. That makes 14 points in his last 10, about twice what we'd expect at his ice time, and our form check calls it earned: his own chances are up too.

Tampa Bay takes 61% of the expected goals (the quality of the chances) at five on five with him on the ice, seven points better than without him. Evolving-Hockey had him worth 2.5 wins last season, 17th among defensemen, driving play even after adjusting for teammates and competition.

The pace won't hold all year (19 points in 21 games sits above any range we'd project for a defenseman his age), and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking flags a weak spot: only 31% of his exits keep possession, so watch for clears off the glass when the forecheck comes. Watch how the Lightning manage his minutes; he's at 19 a night, not 25.
